summary.text: Samantha Mota is a Democratic candidate who placed second in the June 2026 top-two primary and faces fellow Democrat Sydney Kamlager-Dove in the general election. A Los Angeles County native and former Santa Monica commissioner, she describes her campaign as grassroots and community-focused. She has named immigration reform, universal health care, family leave and economic stability as policy priorities.

paragraphs.text: Samantha Mota says she was born and raised in Los Angeles County in a rent-controlled unit, and that her single-parent family relied on WIC, SNAP, Medicaid and other programs.
She attended Santa Monica College for political science, then joined Climate Action Santa Monica and began guerrilla gardening in a vacant lot, which she describes as the start of her activism.
In October 2021, according to her campaign website, the City of Santa Monica's Hispanic Heritage Month Committee gave her its Premio de Orgullo Award for expanding urban agriculture.
Mota was appointed in January 2021 to Santa Monica's Public Safety Reform and Oversight Commission, and she was a candidate for Santa Monica City Council in August 2022.
She says she later moved to Baldwin Hills, where she lives with her husband.

In her 2025 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey, Mota describes her campaign as grassroots, community focused and transparent, and says she is running because of a lack of new and transparent leadership in politics.
She placed second in the June 2, 2026 nonpartisan primary with 11.7% of the vote (15,019 votes), advancing to a same-party general election against incumbent Sydney Kamlager-Dove.
